messages:
emily: hey team, just escalated a production issue from ShopMate — their rerank calls are getting 429s and it's affecting search relevance for customers. reported ~8:12am PT. they say it started after a traffic spike around 8:00am.

emily: customer provided snippet of the error: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"quota_exceeded\",
  \"message\": \"Rerank request quota exceeded for API key\"
}
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 1849500300
```

emily: they also attached a representative request payload (they batch 20 queries in one call):

```
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"queries\": ["query a","query b", ... 20 items],
  \"candidates\": [["doc1","doc2",...], ...]
}
```

lee: I'm looking at dashboard, I can confirm a sharp spike from that org key starting 07:58:14 -> sustained bursts up to 220 QPS for ~3m, aggregated minute rates hit 13k/min which tripped the per-minute cap. Their plan quota is 10k/min for rerank.

akshay: hmm their account is on growth plan with rerank cap 10k/min. The headers show Limit:600 though — that header value is per-request concurrency quota for the legacy rerank endpoint, not the account-level per-minute. We have two layers: per-org per-minute + per-endpoint concurrent buckets. Looks like they hit both intermittently.

dana: could be that their client is doing very narrow exponential retries without jitter so bursts keep aligning and burning the bucket. also noticed some requests return quick 429s with very low latency -> suggests concurrency limit trip, not a slow downstream.

emily: customer timeline: they ramped a new A/B test around 07:50 with aggressive rerank sampling. asked for repro steps to share with infra.

lee: repro steps I used in staging:
1) simulate 200 QPS for 2m using their payload (20 queries per request).
2) observe X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining hitting 0 and subsequent 429s.
3) reduce to 50 QPS, rate becomes healthy again.

```
# quick load test script (example)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test' -d '{"queries":["q1"],"candidates":[["d1","d2"]]}' &
done
```

akshay: immediate mitigations:
- support ask customer to add jitter + exponential backoff for 429s.
- reduce per-request batch size (they batch 20 queries; reduce to 5) to lower burstiness.
- temporary quota bump for their org while we investigate.

emily: I proposed a temporary bump and asked for permission to apply it. customer said yes if we can do a 1 hour window.

lee: I created infra ticket INFRA-7829 to add short-term org quota adjustment workflow + audit log so we can do safe manual bumps.

akshay: I can do the manual bump now. command I ran (audit-only snippet):

```
# admin shim (audit only, replace with real admin ctl in prod)
adminctl quota adjust --org shopmate --metric rerank_per_minute --add 5000 --duration 3600 --reason \"prod incident: rerank 429s\"
```

deploy-bot: quota change queued, awaiting approval from infra-owner.

lee: approved and applied. monitoring shows their X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining stayed >0 after the change for the last 3 minutes. 429 error rate dropped from 18% -> 0.8%.

dana: for long-term: recommend we add a per-key burst allowance smoothing (leaky bucket) and surface guidance in docs: prefer smaller batches or multiplexing multiple queries per second vs bulk bursts. also suggest adding a specific rerank rate-limiter metric on per-org dashboard.

emily: next steps for support: send customer mitigations doc (jitter/backoff, reduce batch size, handle 429), confirm they'll roll back the A/B test to gradual ramp, and schedule a postmortem with infra.

emily: customer on the thread said: \"thanks, the bump stopped the errors, we'll implement backoff and cut batch size. can we get a follow-up to make sure we don't need permanent plan change?\"

akshay: flagging product: we should check the UX for quota guidance on rerank endpoint — current docs mention per-minute quotas but not concurrency headers causes.

lee: logging/todo: attach the raw request IDs and sample 429 responses to INFRA-7829. I'll follow up in the ticket with traces.

emily: I'll close the support case once customer confirms changes tomorrow. marking this resolved-high for now. :white_check_mark:
